exceptions.reason: One removal owner keeps authorization, durable admission, current checks, single dispatch, and conditional terminal receipts in one ordered flow. Its largest function has nine paths. Focused cases cover ambiguous admission, provider uncertainty, completion mismatch, and exact receipt matching. Further splitting would spread the no-replay and completion authority rules without reducing their decisions.

One rule file keeps current actor authority, exact target facts, all grant support, complete bounded member pages, and the last-Admin decision together. Its largest function has nine paths, covered by refusal, pagination, duplicate, and target-change cases. Per-guard files would hide the order that prevents a stale User-to-Admin transition from bypassing the last-Admin check.

One small lifetime owns the total deadline, admission uncertainty, read stop signal, guarded continuations, and one public result. Its largest function has four paths. Tests cover the exact deadline, accumulated phase time, close, late replies, and signal propagation. Splitting timer, stop, or result state into another owner would obscure release-once and no-late-dispatch guarantees.
